decisions.reason: Artemis was the city's own goddess, honored in a huge temple counted among the wonders of the ancient world. She shared her name with the Greek goddess of hunting, but at Ephesus she was worshiped as a great mother goddess. The King James Version calls her by her Roman name, Diana.

decisions.choice: silver shrines: small models of the shrine or temple of Artemis, sold to worshipers
alternatives: silver offerings made for the temple
decisions.reason: The word means a temple or the inner shrine where a god's image stood. Small clay and marble shrines of Artemis are known, but none in silver has been found, so exactly what Demetrius made is not certain.

decisions.choice: Men: Demetrius speaks to the craftsmen and workmen of his trade
decisions.reason: The hearers are the workers of a trade that Demetrius has called together, and the address fits them as they were, so it is kept as it is.

decisions.choice: persuaded and turned away: won people over and drew them from the worship of the gods
alternatives: changed their minds on a small matter
decisions.reason: The second verb means to move someone from one place to another. Demetrius means that people stopped worshiping the gods of the city.

decisions.choice: gods made with hands are not gods: Paul's teaching about idols
decisions.reason: Paul said the same in Athens (17:24-29). Believers in Thessalonica had turned from idols to the living God (1 Thessalonians 1:9).

decisions.choice: small silver models of the shrine of the goddess Artemis
decisions.reason: Readable says what the shrines most likely were, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: we make a lot of money; turning away from our gods
alternatives: our wealth is from this business; turned away a large crowd
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what Demetrius means by wealth and what the people turned from, as the meaning notes explain.

decisions.choice: Hommes (L); Hommes de métier (B); Mes amis (R)
decisions.reason: A bare "Hommes" as an address is stiff in modern French. Literal keeps it; Balanced says whom Demetrius is addressing, the men of his trade (m3); Readable uses the natural friendly address. "Messieurs" would sound like a modern business meeting.

decisions.choice: orfèvre
decisions.reason: "Orfèvre" is the French word for a craftsman who works gold and silver; the text says what he made, so the metal is clear.

decisions.choice: Artemisa
decisions.reason: The usual modern Spanish name of the Greek goddess (meaning decision on Artemis); "Diana" is her Roman name, which the Greek text does not use. The same through 19:35.

decisions.choice: Compañeros
decisions.reason: Demetrius speaks to men of his own trade (meaning decision on "Men"); Spanish "Hombres" or "Varones" as a form of address sounds odd here, and "Compañeros" says who they are. The word has no gender span, as the English has none.

decisions.choice: vihekalu vya fedha vya Artemi (L, B); vinyago vidogo vya fedha vya hekalu la mungu wa kike Artemi (R)
decisions.reason: The small silver models of her shrine (meaning decision), with the diminutive "vi-" of "hekalu"; the goddess is named "Artemi" from her Greek name, as "Zeusi" and "Herme" in 14:12, not with the Latin "Diana".

decisions.choice: Wanaume (L); Wenzangu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Demetrius speaks to the men of his own trade (meaning decision), so Literal keeps "Wanaume" and Balanced and Readable use the address a man uses to fellow workers, "Wenzangu" (my colleagues).

source.text: οὐ μόνον δὲ τοῦτο κινδυνεύει ἡμῖν τὸ μέρος εἰς ἀπελεγμὸν ἐλθεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ τῆς μεγάλης θεᾶς Ἀρτέμιδος ἱερὸν εἰς οὐθὲν λογισθῆναι, μέλλειν τε καὶ καθαιρεῖσθαι τῆς μεγαλειότητος αὐτῆς, ἣν ὅλη ἡ Ἀσία καὶ ἡ οἰκουμένη σέβεται.

records.literal_gloss: Not only but this is endangered to us the part into disrepute to come, but also the of the great goddess Artemis temple for nothing to be reckoned, to be about also to be deposed of the majesty of her, whom all the Asia and the world worships.

en.L: And not only is there danger for us that this trade of ours will come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and that she whom all Asia and the world worships is about to be brought down from her majesty."
en.B: It is not only that our trade risks being despised. The temple of the great goddess Artemis may come to count for nothing, and she, the goddess whom all Asia and the whole world worship, may soon be pulled down from her greatness."
en.R: There is a danger that people will stop respecting our business. But that is not all. People will also think that the temple of the great goddess Artemis is worth nothing. Everyone in Asia and in the whole world worships her. But soon she will not seem great anymore!"

fr.L: Et non seulement il y a danger pour nous que notre métier tombe dans le discrédit, mais aussi que le temple de la grande déesse Artémis soit compté pour rien, et qu’elle soit sur le point d’être déchue de sa majesté, elle que toute l’Asie et le monde vénèrent. »
fr.B: Ce n’est pas seulement notre métier qui risque d’être méprisé. Le temple de la grande déesse Artémis risque d’être tenu pour rien, et elle, la déesse que toute l’Asie et le monde entier adorent, pourrait bientôt être dépouillée de sa grandeur. »
fr.R: Il y a un danger : les gens vont cesser de respecter notre commerce. Mais ce n’est pas tout. Les gens vont aussi penser que le temple de la grande déesse Artémis ne vaut rien. Tout le monde, en Asie et dans le monde entier, adore Artémis. Mais bientôt, elle ne paraîtra plus grande du tout ! »

es.L: Y no solo hay peligro de que este oficio nuestro caiga en descrédito, sino también de que el templo de la gran diosa Artemisa sea tenido por nada, y que esté a punto de ser despojada de su majestad aquella a quien toda Asia y el mundo adoran».
es.B: No solo corremos el peligro de que nuestro oficio caiga en descrédito. También el templo de la gran diosa Artemisa puede llegar a no valer nada, y ella, la diosa a quien adoran toda Asia y el mundo entero, pronto puede ser despojada de su grandeza».
es.R: Hay peligro de que la gente deje de respetar nuestro negocio. Pero eso no es todo. La gente también va a pensar que el templo de la gran diosa Artemisa no vale nada. Todos en Asia y en el mundo entero la adoran. ¡Pero pronto ya no parecerá grande!».

sw.L: Na si tu kwamba kuna hatari kwetu kwamba kazi hii yetu itadharauliwa, bali pia kwamba hekalu la mungu wa kike mkuu Artemi litahesabiwa si kitu, na kwamba yeye ambaye Asia yote na ulimwengu wote unamwabudu yu karibu kuondolewa katika ukuu wake."
sw.B: Si kwamba kazi yetu tu iko hatarini kudharauliwa. Hekalu la mungu wa kike mkuu Artemi linaweza kuonekana si kitu, naye, mungu wa kike ambaye Asia yote na ulimwengu wote humwabudu, anaweza kushushwa upesi kutoka katika ukuu wake."
sw.R: Kuna hatari kwamba watu wataacha kuiheshimu biashara yetu. Lakini si hivyo tu. Watu watafikiri pia kwamba hekalu la mungu wa kike mkuu Artemi halina thamani yoyote. Kila mtu katika Asia na katika ulimwengu wote humwabudu Artemi. Lakini hivi karibuni hataonekana tena kuwa mkuu!"

decisions.choice: this part: our trade, our line of work
decisions.reason: The word means a part or share, and here the business that is theirs.

decisions.choice: the temple of the great goddess Artemis: her great temple outside Ephesus
decisions.reason: Her temple at Ephesus was counted among the seven wonders of the ancient world.

decisions.choice: all Asia and the world worship her: a proud boast
decisions.reason: Demetrius speaks with pride for his city. Her worship was indeed widespread around the Mediterranean, but he is stirring up his hearers.

decisions.choice: Demetrius moves from money to religion
decisions.reason: "Not only ... but also" sets the danger to their trade beside the danger to the goddess. The second sounds nobler, but it is joined to the first.

source.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ καὶ γενόμενοι πλήρεις θυμοῦ ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then and having become full of rage they were crying out, saying, Great [is] the Artemis of Ephesians!

en.L: And when they heard [this] and were filled with rage, they cried out, saying, "Great [is] Artemis of [the] Ephesians!"
en.B: On hearing this they flew into a rage, and they kept shouting, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
en.R: When the men heard this, they became very angry. They began to shout, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

fr.L: Et ayant entendu [cela] et étant devenus pleins de fureur, ils criaient, disant : « Grande [est] l’Artémis des Éphésiens ! »
fr.B: À ces mots, ils furent remplis de fureur et ne cessaient de crier : « Grande est l’Artémis des Éphésiens ! »
fr.R: Quand les hommes ont entendu cela, ils sont devenus furieux. Ils ont commencé à crier : « Grande est l’Artémis des Éphésiens ! »

es.L: Y al oír [esto], llenos de furia, gritaban diciendo: «¡Grande [es] la Artemisa de [los] efesios!».
es.B: Al oír esto, se llenaron de furia y se pusieron a gritar: «¡Grande es la Artemisa de los efesios!».
es.R: Cuando los hombres oyeron esto, se enojaron mucho. Empezaron a gritar: «¡Grande es la Artemisa de los efesios!».

sw.L: Na waliposikia [hayo] na kujaa ghadhabu, walikuwa wakipiga kelele, wakisema, "Mkuu [ni] Artemi wa Waefeso!"
sw.B: Waliposikia hayo, walijawa na hasira kali, wakaendelea kupiga kelele, "Artemi wa Waefeso ni mkuu!"
sw.R: Wale watu waliposikia hayo, walikasirika sana. Wakaanza kupiga kelele, "Artemi wa Waefeso ni mkuu!"

decisions.choice: Great is Artemis of the Ephesians: a cry of praise to the city's goddess
decisions.reason: "Great" was a title given to Artemis of Ephesus. The words were both worship and civic pride.

decisions.choice: they were crying out: they kept on shouting
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes a cry that went on and on, as in 19:34.

source.text: καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ πόλις τῆς συγχύσεως, ὥρμησάν τε ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον συναρπάσαντες Γάϊον καὶ Ἀρίσταρχον Μακεδόνας, συνεκδήμους Παύλου.

records.literal_gloss: And was filled the city with the confusion, they rushed and with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, fellow travelers of Paul.

en.L: And the city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, Paul's traveling companions.
en.B: Confusion spread through the city, and with one impulse the people stormed into the theater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, the Macedonians who traveled with Paul.
en.R: Soon the whole city was full of confusion. People grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, two men from Macedonia who were traveling with Paul. Then the crowd all ran together into the theater.

fr.L: Et la ville fut remplie de confusion, et ils se précipitèrent d’un même élan au théâtre, ayant entraîné Gaïus et Aristarque, Macédoniens, compagnons de voyage de Paul.
fr.B: La confusion gagna toute la ville, et d’un même élan la foule se rua au théâtre, entraînant Gaïus et Aristarque, les Macédoniens qui voyageaient avec Paul.
fr.R: Bientôt, toute la ville a été pleine d’agitation. Des gens ont attrapé Gaïus et Aristarque, deux hommes de Macédoine qui voyageaient avec Paul. Puis toute la foule a couru ensemble au théâtre.

es.L: Y la ciudad se llenó de confusión, y se lanzaron a una al teatro, arrastrando consigo a Gayo y a Aristarco, macedonios, compañeros de viaje de Pablo.
es.B: La confusión se extendió por toda la ciudad, y todos a una se precipitaron al teatro, arrastrando a Gayo y a Aristarco, los macedonios que viajaban con Pablo.
es.R: Pronto toda la ciudad estaba llena de confusión. La gente agarró a Gayo y a Aristarco, dos hombres de Macedonia que viajaban con Pablo. Luego toda la multitud corrió junta al teatro.

sw.L: Na mji ukajaa machafuko, nao wakakimbilia kwa nia moja katika ukumbi wa michezo, wakiwa wamewakamata Gayo na Aristarko, Wamakedonia, wenzi wa safari wa Paulo.
sw.B: Machafuko yakaenea mjini kote, na watu wakakimbilia kwa pamoja ndani ya ukumbi wa michezo, wakiwaburuta Gayo na Aristarko, Wamakedonia waliosafiri pamoja na Paulo.
sw.R: Mara mji wote ukajaa machafuko. Watu waliwakamata Gayo na Aristarko, watu wawili kutoka Makedonia waliokuwa wakisafiri pamoja na Paulo. Kisha umati wote ukakimbilia pamoja ndani ya ukumbi wa michezo.

decisions.choice: the theater: the city's great open-air theater, where public assemblies met
decisions.reason: The theater of Ephesus held about 24,000 people. Its ruins can still be seen. Cities used their theaters for meetings of the citizens.

decisions.choice: with one accord: all together, with one impulse
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the crowd that rushed at Stephen (7:57) and of the believers praying together (1:14).

decisions.choice: Gaius and Aristarchus: two of Paul's companions from Macedonia
decisions.reason: Aristarchus came from Thessalonica (20:4, 27:2) and was later with Paul in prison (Colossians 4:10). Gaius was a common name; the Gaius of Derbe in 20:4 may be another man.

decisions.choice: people grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus; then the crowd all ran into the theater
alternatives: they rushed into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events one at a time.

decisions.choice: ukumbi wa michezo
decisions.reason: The city's great open-air theater, where assemblies met (meaning decision); "ukumbi wa michezo" (hall for shows) is plain Swahili for a theater, where "thieta" would be a loanword few readers know. The same in 19:31.

source.text: Παύλου δὲ βουλομένου εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον οὐκ εἴων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταί·

records.literal_gloss: Of Paul however intending to go in to the people, not were allowing him the disciples.

en.L: But when Paul wanted to go in to the people, the disciples would not allow him.
en.B: Paul was ready to go in and face the assembled people, but the disciples kept him from doing so.
en.R: Paul wanted to go into the theater and speak to the crowd. But the followers of Jesus would not let him.

fr.L: Mais comme Paul voulait entrer vers le peuple, les disciples ne le laissaient pas [faire].
fr.B: Paul était prêt à entrer pour affronter le peuple assemblé, mais les disciples l’en empêchèrent.
fr.R: Paul voulait entrer dans le théâtre et parler à la foule. Mais ceux qui suivaient Jésus ne l’ont pas laissé faire.

es.L: Y queriendo Pablo entrar ante el pueblo, los discípulos no se lo permitían.
es.B: Pablo quería entrar para presentarse ante la asamblea del pueblo, pero los discípulos no lo dejaron.
es.R: Pablo quería entrar al teatro y hablar a la multitud. Pero los discípulos no lo dejaron.

sw.L: Lakini Paulo alipotaka kuingia kwa watu, wanafunzi hawakumruhusu.
sw.B: Paulo alikuwa tayari kuingia na kuwakabili watu waliokusanyika, lakini wanafunzi walimzuia.
sw.R: Paulo alitaka kuingia ndani ya ukumbi wa michezo na kuzungumza na umati. Lakini wanafunzi hawakumruhusu.

decisions.choice: the people: the citizens gathered as an assembly
decisions.reason: The word is used of a city's citizen body meeting together (12:22, 17:5).

decisions.choice: would not allow: kept him back
decisions.reason: The imperfect suggests they went on holding him back.

decisions.choice: go into the theater and speak to the crowd
decisions.reason: Readable says where Paul wanted to go and why.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says who the disciples were.

source.text: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἀσιαρχῶν, ὄντες αὐτῷ φίλοι, πέμψαντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παρεκάλουν μὴ δοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον.

records.literal_gloss: Some then also of the Asiarchs, being to him friends, having sent to him were urging not to give himself into the theater.

en.L: And some of the Asiarchs also, being his friends, sent to him and were urging [him] not to venture into the theater.
en.B: Some of the Asiarchs, too, who were his friends, sent word to him and pleaded with him not to put himself at risk in the theater.
en.R: Some of the leading officials of the province were Paul's friends. They sent a message to him. They begged him not to go into the theater.

fr.L: Et même quelques-uns des Asiarques, qui étaient ses amis, envoyèrent [quelqu’un] vers lui et le priaient de ne pas s’aventurer dans le théâtre.
fr.B: Quelques-uns des Asiarques, qui étaient de ses amis, lui envoyèrent aussi un message pour le supplier de ne pas s’exposer au théâtre.
fr.R: Quelques-uns des principaux dirigeants de la province étaient des amis de Paul. Ils lui ont envoyé un message. Ils l’ont supplié de ne pas aller au théâtre.

es.L: Y también algunos de los asiarcas, que eran amigos suyos, enviaron [a decirle] y le rogaban que no se presentara en el teatro.
es.B: Además, algunos de los asiarcas, que eran amigos suyos, le mandaron recado rogándole que no se arriesgara a ir al teatro.
es.R: Algunos de los funcionarios más importantes de la provincia eran amigos de Pablo. Le enviaron un mensaje. Le rogaron que no fuera al teatro.

sw.L: Na baadhi ya Asiarki pia, waliokuwa rafiki zake, walimtumia [ujumbe], wakimsihi asijitokeze katika ukumbi wa michezo.
sw.B: Baadhi ya viongozi mashuhuri wa Asia pia, waliokuwa rafiki zake, walimtumia ujumbe wakimsihi asijihatarishe kwa kuingia katika ukumbi wa michezo.
sw.R: Baadhi ya maafisa wakuu wa jimbo walikuwa rafiki za Paulo. Walimtumia ujumbe. Wakamsihi asiingie katika ukumbi wa michezo.

decisions.choice: Asiarchs: leading wealthy men of the province of Asia, who bore a title of honor
decisions.reason: The title appears in many inscriptions from Asia. Asiarchs were men of wealth and standing, linked with the provincial council and its festivals, but their exact duties are not certain.

decisions.choice: not to give himself into the theater: not to risk going in
decisions.reason: To give oneself into a place means to venture there, at one's own risk.

decisions.choice: being his friends: some of the city's leading men were friendly to Paul
decisions.reason: Luke shows that people of standing did not see Paul as a danger.

decisions.choice: the leading officials of the province
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: les Asiarques
alternatives: les dirigeants de la province d’Asie
decisions.reason: French keeps the title, as the English does at Literal and Balanced; Readable explains it (m1).

decisions.choice: los asiarcas
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Greek title, the leading men of the province (meaning decision on Asiarchs), as the English does; Readable says who they were.

decisions.choice: Asiarki (L); viongozi mashuhuri wa Asia (B); maafisa wakuu wa jimbo (R)
decisions.reason: Leading wealthy men of the province who bore a title of honor (meaning decision): Literal keeps the title as a loanword, Balanced and Readable say who they were.

source.text: ἄλλοι μὲν οὖν ἄλλο τι ἔκραζον, ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἐκκλησία συγκεχυμένη, καὶ οἱ πλείους οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τίνος ἕνεκα συνεληλύθεισαν.

records.literal_gloss: Others indeed therefore something other were crying out, was for the assembly confused, and the most not did know for what cause they had come together.

en.L: So some were crying out one thing and some another, for the assembly was confused, and most did not know for what reason they had come together.
en.B: Meanwhile people shouted all kinds of things, some one thing and some another. The assembly was in chaos, and most of them had no idea what had brought them there.
en.R: People were shouting different things. The whole assembly was confused. Most of them did not know the reason they had all gathered.

fr.L: Les uns donc criaient une chose, les autres une autre, car l’assemblée était en confusion, et la plupart ne savaient pas pour quelle raison ils s’étaient réunis.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, on criait toutes sortes de choses, les uns ceci, les autres cela. L’assemblée était en plein désordre, et la plupart ne savaient même pas pourquoi ils étaient là.
fr.R: Les gens criaient des choses différentes. Toute l’assemblée était dans la confusion. La plupart d’entre eux ne savaient pas pourquoi ils s’étaient tous réunis.

es.L: Así que unos gritaban una cosa y otros otra, porque la asamblea estaba confusa, y la mayoría no sabía por qué se habían reunido.
es.B: Mientras tanto, unos gritaban una cosa y otros otra. La asamblea era un caos, y la mayoría ni sabía para qué estaba allí.
es.R: La gente gritaba cosas diferentes. Toda la asamblea estaba confundida. La mayoría no sabía por qué se habían reunido todos.

sw.L: Basi wengine walikuwa wakipiga kelele hili na wengine lile, kwa maana mkutano ulikuwa umevurugika, na wengi hawakujua ni kwa sababu gani walikuwa wamekusanyika.
sw.B: Wakati huo watu walipiga kelele za kila aina, wengine hili na wengine lile. Mkutano ulikuwa na machafuko, na wengi wao hawakujua ni nini kilichowaleta pale.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wakipiga kelele mambo tofauti. Mkutano wote ulikuwa umechanganyikiwa. Wengi wao hawakujua sababu ya kukusanyika kwao.

decisions.choice: assembly: the gathering of the people of the city, here a disorderly one
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary Greek name for a city's assembly of citizens. Luke uses it of the believers (5:11) and of Israel in the desert (7:38); here it is the crowd in the theater, which the town clerk sets beside the lawful assembly (19:39).

decisions.choice: some one thing, some another: a babble of shouts
decisions.reason: Each shouted something different, as in 21:34.

decisions.choice: for: explains the shouting
decisions.reason: The crowd shouted different things because no one knew what was going on.

decisions.choice: l’assemblée
decisions.reason: Here the Greek word for "church" names the gathering of the city's people (m1), so French says "l’assemblée", as in 19:39 and 19:40, and never "l’Église".

decisions.choice: la asamblea
decisions.reason: The Greek word that elsewhere names the church here names the gathering of the city's people (meaning decision on assembly); Spanish says "asamblea", as in 19:39 and 19:40.

decisions.choice: mkutano
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the church, but here it means the gathering of the city's people (meaning decision), so Swahili says "mkutano" (assembly); the same in 19:39-40.

source.text: ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ὄχλου συνεβίβασαν Ἀλέξανδρον προβαλόντων αὐτὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὁ δὲ Ἀλέξανδρος κατασείσας τὴν χεῖρα ἤθελεν ἀπολογεῖσθαι τῷ δήμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Out of now the crowd they instructed Alexander, having put forward him the Jews; the and Alexander having motioned the hand was wanting to make a defense to the people.

en.L: And some out of the crowd instructed Alexander, the Jews having put him forward; and Alexander, motioning with his hand, wanted to make a defense to the people.
en.B: Some of the crowd told Alexander what to say, since the Jews had pushed him forward, and Alexander signaled with his hand, intending to speak in his own defense to the people.
en.R: The Jews pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd, and some people told him what to say. Alexander raised his hand to get the people to be quiet. He wanted to speak to the crowd and defend himself.

fr.L: Et du milieu de la foule, on instruisit Alexandre, les Juifs l’ayant poussé en avant ; et Alexandre, ayant fait signe de la main, voulait présenter une défense au peuple.
fr.B: Quelques-uns, dans la foule, firent la leçon à Alexandre, que les Juifs avaient poussé en avant, et Alexandre fit signe de la main ; il voulait présenter sa défense devant le peuple.
fr.R: Les Juifs ont poussé un homme appelé Alexandre devant la foule, et certaines personnes lui ont dit ce qu’il devait dire. Alexandre a levé la main pour que les gens se taisent. Il voulait parler à la foule et se défendre.

es.L: Y de entre la multitud instruyeron a Alejandro, empujándolo los judíos hacia delante; y Alejandro, haciendo señal con la mano, quería presentar una defensa ante el pueblo.
es.B: Algunos de la multitud le dijeron a Alejandro qué decir, porque los judíos lo habían empujado al frente. Alejandro hizo una señal con la mano, con intención de hablar en su defensa ante el pueblo.
es.R: Los judíos empujaron hacia el frente de la multitud a un hombre llamado Alejandro, y algunas personas le dijeron lo que tenía que decir. Alejandro levantó la mano para que la gente se callara. Quería hablar a la multitud y defenderse.

sw.L: Na baadhi ya umati walimwelekeza Aleksanda, Wayahudi wakiwa wamemsukuma mbele; naye Aleksanda, akiashiria kwa mkono, alitaka kujitetea mbele ya watu.
sw.B: Baadhi ya watu katika umati walimweleza Aleksanda la kusema, kwa kuwa Wayahudi walikuwa wamemsukuma mbele. Aleksanda akaashiria kwa mkono, akitaka kujitetea mbele ya watu.
sw.R: Wayahudi walimsukuma mtu mmoja aitwaye Aleksanda mbele ya umati, na watu fulani wakamweleza la kusema. Aleksanda aliinua mkono wake ili watu wanyamaze. Alitaka kuzungumza na umati na kujitetea.

decisions.choice: instructed: told him what to say
alternatives: concluded that Alexander was the cause
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to instruct, or to put things together and conclude. Some manuscripts have another verb meaning to bring forward, which the King James Version follows ("drew Alexander out"). Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Jews put him forward: probably to show that the Jews had no part in Paul's teaching
decisions.reason: Jews also refused to worship idols, and the crowd might blame them along with Paul. Luke does not say what Alexander meant to say. It is not certain that he is the Alexander of 1 Timothy 1:20 or 2 Timothy 4:14.

decisions.choice: motioned with his hand: a speaker's sign asking for silence
decisions.reason: Peter and Paul do the same before speaking (12:17, 13:16, 21:40).

decisions.choice: to get the people to be quiet
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν φωνὴ ἐγένετο μία ἐκ πάντων ὡς ἐπὶ ὥρας δύο κραζόντων· Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.

records.literal_gloss: Having recognized however that a Jew he is, a cry there was one from all, about for hours two crying out, Great [is] the Artemis of Ephesians!

en.L: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, one cry arose from them all, as for about two hours they cried out, "Great [is] Artemis of [the] Ephesians!"
en.B: But as soon as they realized he was a Jew, they all joined in one shout, and for about two hours they cried out, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
en.R: But the crowd saw that Alexander was a Jew. So they all began to shout together, and they kept on shouting for about two hours, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

fr.L: Mais quand ils reconnurent qu’il était juif, une seule voix s’éleva de tous, qui crièrent pendant environ deux heures : « Grande [est] l’Artémis des Éphésiens ! »
fr.B: Mais dès qu’ils comprirent qu’il était juif, tous se mirent à crier d’une seule voix, et pendant environ deux heures ils hurlèrent : « Grande est l’Artémis des Éphésiens ! »
fr.R: Mais la foule a vu qu’Alexandre était juif. Alors tous ont commencé à crier ensemble, et ils ont continué à crier pendant environ deux heures : « Grande est l’Artémis des Éphésiens ! »

es.L: Pero al reconocer que era judío, se levantó un solo grito de todos, que durante unas dos horas gritaban: «¡Grande [es] la Artemisa de [los] efesios!».
es.B: Pero en cuanto se dieron cuenta de que era judío, todos se unieron en un solo grito, y durante unas dos horas estuvieron gritando: «¡Grande es la Artemisa de los efesios!».
es.R: Pero la gente vio que Alejandro era judío. Entonces todos empezaron a gritar a la vez, y siguieron gritando durante unas dos horas: «¡Grande es la Artemisa de los efesios!».

sw.L: Lakini walipotambua kwamba yeye ni Myahudi, sauti moja ilitoka kwa wote, wakipiga kelele kwa muda wa kama saa mbili, "Mkuu [ni] Artemi wa Waefeso!"
sw.B: Lakini mara walipotambua kwamba ni Myahudi, wote walipaza sauti moja, na kwa muda wa kama saa mbili wakapiga kelele, "Artemi wa Waefeso ni mkuu!"
sw.R: Lakini umati ulipoona kwamba Aleksanda ni Myahudi, wote walianza kupiga kelele pamoja. Wakaendelea kupiga kelele kwa muda wa kama saa mbili, "Artemi wa Waefeso ni mkuu!"

decisions.choice: a Jew: one who would not worship Artemis
decisions.reason: Jews refused to worship idols, so the crowd took Alexander to be against their goddess too.

decisions.choice: the sentence changes its grammar part way: they recognized ... one cry from all
decisions.reason: The opening participle does not fit the rest of the sentence. The broken grammar suits the excited scene.

decisions.choice: the crowd; Alexander
decisions.reason: Readable names who saw whom.

source.text: καταστείλας δὲ ὁ γραμματεὺς τὸν ὄχλον φησίν· Ἄνδρες Ἐφέσιοι, τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἀνθρώπων ὃς οὐ γινώσκει τὴν Ἐφεσίων πόλιν νεωκόρον οὖσαν τῆς μεγάλης Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τοῦ διοπετοῦς;

records.literal_gloss: Having calmed then the town clerk the crowd says, Men Ephesians, who for is there of men who not knows the of Ephesians city temple keeper being of the great Artemis and of the fallen from heaven?

en.L: And when the town clerk had quieted the crowd, he said, "Men, Ephesians, who is there among {{gender:people|men}} who does not know that the city of [the] Ephesians is temple keeper of the great Artemis and of the [image] fallen from heaven?
en.B: The town clerk managed to quiet the crowd and said, "{{gender:People|Men}} of Ephesus, is there anyone at all who does not know that this city of the Ephesians has been entrusted with the temple of the great Artemis and with the image that fell from heaven?
en.R: Finally the town clerk got the crowd to be quiet. He said, "People of Ephesus, everyone knows that our city takes care of the temple of the great goddess Artemis. Everyone knows that we also guard her image that fell from heaven.

fr.L: Et le secrétaire, ayant calmé la foule, déclare : « Hommes éphésiens, qui donc y a-t-il parmi les {{gender:humains|hommes}} qui ne sache que la ville des Éphésiens est gardienne du temple de la grande Artémis et de [la statue] tombée du ciel ?
fr.B: Le secrétaire de la ville parvint à calmer la foule et dit : « {{gender:Éphésiens|Hommes d’Éphèse}}, y a-t-il quelqu’un qui ignore que la ville des Éphésiens a reçu la garde du temple de la grande Artémis et de la statue tombée du ciel ?
fr.R: Finalement, le secrétaire de la ville a réussi à faire taire la foule. Il a dit : « Habitants d’Éphèse, tout le monde sait que notre ville s’occupe du temple de la grande déesse Artémis. Tout le monde sait aussi que nous gardons sa statue tombée du ciel.

es.L: Y habiendo calmado el secretario de la ciudad a la multitud, dijo: «Varones efesios, ¿quién hay entre {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que no sepa que la ciudad de [los] efesios es guardiana del templo de la gran Artemisa y de la [imagen] caída del cielo?
es.B: El secretario de la ciudad logró calmar a la multitud y dijo: «{{gender:Habitantes de Éfeso|Varones efesios}}, ¿hay alguien que no sepa que a esta ciudad de los efesios se le ha confiado el templo de la gran Artemisa y la imagen que cayó del cielo?
es.R: Por fin, el secretario de la ciudad logró que la multitud se callara. Dijo: «Habitantes de Éfeso, todos saben que nuestra ciudad cuida el templo de la gran diosa Artemisa. Todos saben que también guardamos su imagen, la que cayó del cielo.

sw.L: Na karani wa mji alipokwisha kuutuliza umati, anasema, "Wanaume, Waefeso, ni nani kati ya wanadamu asiyejua kwamba mji wa Waefeso ni mlinzi wa hekalu la Artemi mkuu na wa [sanamu] iliyoanguka kutoka mbinguni?
sw.B: Karani wa mji aliweza kuutuliza umati, akasema, "Enyi watu wa Efeso, je, kuna mtu yeyote asiyejua kwamba mji huu wa Waefeso umekabidhiwa ulinzi wa hekalu la Artemi mkuu, na wa sanamu iliyoanguka kutoka mbinguni?
sw.R: Mwishowe karani wa mji aliufanya umati unyamaze. Akasema, "Enyi watu wa Efeso, kila mtu anajua kwamba mji wetu unalitunza hekalu la mungu wa kike mkuu Artemi. Kila mtu anajua kwamba sisi pia tunailinda sanamu yake iliyoanguka kutoka mbinguni.

decisions.choice: the town clerk: the city's leading official, who kept its records and dealt with the assembly
alternatives: a scribe who taught the law
a clerk who only wrote letters
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the Jewish scribes, but in a Greek city it was the title of the chief official. Inscriptions from Ephesus show him drafting the assembly's decrees and acting for the city before the Roman authorities.

decisions.choice: Men of Ephesus: the formal address to the citizens, said here to a mixed crowd
decisions.reason: This was the usual way to address the citizen assembly. The crowd in the theater was a gathering of the city, likely men and women together.

decisions.choice: temple keeper: the city's title of honor as guardian of a temple
decisions.reason: The word first meant a temple warden. Inscriptions and coins of Ephesus use it as the city's proud title, guardian of Artemis's temple.

decisions.choice: the image fallen from heaven: a sacred object believed to have fallen from the sky
alternatives: the statue of Artemis made by human hands
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "the fallen from heaven" and leaves the noun to be understood. Most likely it was an image of Artemis believed to have come from the sky, perhaps a meteorite. The clerk answers the charge that gods made with hands are not gods (19:26): this one, he claims, no human hand made.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: People of Ephesus, with "Men of Ephesus" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 3:12, for a mixed crowd; the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: two plain statements
decisions.reason: Readable states what the clerk's question implies.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Éphésiens|Hommes d’Éphèse}}
decisions.reason: As the English "People of Ephesus": the clerk addresses a mixed crowd (m2). French "Éphésiens" alone already includes everyone, and the traditional "Hommes d’Éphèse" is the alternative.

decisions.choice: le secrétaire (de la ville)
decisions.reason: The official kept the city's records and presided over its assembly (m1); "secrétaire de la ville" says this plainly, where "greffier" suggests a court clerk. Literal keeps the present "déclare" of the Greek.

decisions.choice: Varones efesios (L); {{gender:Habitantes de Éfeso|Varones efesios}} (B); Habitantes de Éfeso (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, and as "Varones atenienses" in 17:22: Literal keeps the formal address to the citizens, Balanced has the gender setting, and Readable speaks to the mixed crowd (meaning decision on "Men of Ephesus").

decisions.choice: el secretario de la ciudad
decisions.reason: The city's leading official, who kept its records and dealt with the assembly (meaning decision on the town clerk); "escribano" would suggest a notary, and "escriba" is kept for the Jewish scribes.

decisions.choice: Wanaume, Waefeso (L); Enyi watu wa Efeso (B, R); wanadamu (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The formal address to the citizens, said to a mixed crowd (meaning decision). Literal keeps "Wanaume" as 1:16 does; Balanced and Readable say "Enyi watu wa Efeso", which already includes everyone, so the English gender spans have no Swahili counterpart. Literal "anasema" keeps the Greek present.

decisions.choice: karani wa mji
decisions.reason: The city's leading official, who kept its records (meaning decision); "karani" (clerk) is the plain word, where "mwandishi" is kept for the scribes.

source.text: ἀναντιρρήτων οὖν ὄντων τούτων δέον ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς κατεσταλμένους ὑπάρχειν καὶ μηδὲν προπετὲς πράσσειν.

records.literal_gloss: Undeniable therefore being these things, necessary it is you calm to be and nothing rash to do.

en.L: Since these things are undeniable, then, it is necessary for you to be calm and to do nothing rash.
en.B: No one can dispute these facts, so you ought to keep calm and not do anything reckless.
en.R: No one can say these things are not true. So you need to calm down. Do not do anything foolish without thinking.

fr.L: Ces choses étant donc incontestables, il faut que vous soyez calmes et que vous ne fassiez rien d’inconsidéré.
fr.B: Personne ne peut contester ces faits ; vous devez donc rester calmes et ne rien faire d’irréfléchi.
fr.R: Personne ne peut dire que ce n’est pas vrai. Alors calmez-vous. N’agissez pas sans réfléchir.

es.L: Siendo, pues, estas cosas innegables, es necesario que {{plural_you:ustedes estén|vosotros estéis}} calmados y que no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} nada precipitado.
es.B: Nadie puede negar estos hechos, así que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} mantener la calma y no hacer nada imprudente.
es.R: Nadie puede decir que esto no es verdad. Así que {{plural_you:necesitan calmarse|necesitáis calmaros}}. No {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} nada sin pensar.

sw.L: Basi kwa kuwa mambo haya hayakanushiki, imewapasa kutulia na kutofanya lolote kwa haraka.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kuyapinga mambo haya, kwa hiyo imewapasa kutulia, wala msifanye jambo lolote la pupa.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kusema kwamba mambo haya si kweli. Kwa hiyo mnahitaji kutulia. Msifanye jambo lolote la kijinga bila kufikiri.

decisions.choice: since these things cannot be denied: the clerk reasons from the city's honor
decisions.reason: His point is that Artemis's standing is secure, so there is no need for a riot.

decisions.choice: rash: reckless, done in haste
decisions.reason: The word means falling headlong, acting without thought.

source.text: ἠγάγετε γὰρ τοὺς ἄνδρας τούτους οὔτε ἱεροσύλους οὔτε βλασφημοῦντας τὴν θεὸν ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: You brought for the men these neither temple robbers nor blaspheming the goddess of us.

en.L: For you have brought these men, [who are] neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.
en.B: These men you have dragged here are not temple robbers, and they have not insulted our goddess.
en.R: You brought these men here, but they have not robbed any temple. They have not said bad things about our goddess either.

fr.L: Car vous avez amené ces hommes, [qui ne sont] ni pilleurs de temples ni blasphémateurs de notre déesse.
fr.B: Ces hommes que vous avez traînés ici ne sont pas des pilleurs de temples, et ils n’ont pas insulté notre déesse.
fr.R: Vous avez amené ces hommes ici, mais ils n’ont volé aucun temple. Et ils n’ont pas non plus dit de mal de notre déesse.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:han traído|habéis traído}} a estos hombres, que no son ni ladrones de templos ni blasfemos contra nuestra diosa.
es.B: Estos hombres que {{plural_you:han arrastrado|habéis arrastrado}} hasta aquí no han robado templos ni han insultado a nuestra diosa.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes trajeron|Vosotros trajisteis}} a estos hombres aquí, pero ellos no han robado nada de ningún templo. Tampoco han dicho cosas malas de nuestra diosa.

sw.L: Kwa maana mmewaleta watu hawa, [ambao] si wanyang'anyi wa mahekalu wala si wanaomtukana mungu wetu wa kike.
sw.B: Watu hawa mliowaleta hapa si wezi wa mahekalu, wala hawajamtukana mungu wetu wa kike.
sw.R: Mmewaleta watu hawa hapa, lakini hawajaiba katika hekalu lolote. Wala hawajasema mabaya kuhusu mungu wetu wa kike.

decisions.choice: temple robbers: people who steal from temples or commit sacrilege
decisions.reason: Paul uses the related verb in Romans 2:22. Robbing a temple was counted a grave crime.

decisions.choice: blaspheming our goddess: speaking insults against her
decisions.reason: Paul and his companions taught that idols are not gods (19:26), but they had not insulted Artemis.

decisions.choice: these men: Gaius and Aristarchus
decisions.reason: The crowd had dragged Gaius and Aristarchus into the theater (19:29).

source.text: εἰ μὲν οὖν Δημήτριος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ τεχνῖται ἔχουσιν πρός τινα λόγον, ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται καὶ ἀνθύπατοί εἰσιν, ἐγκαλείτωσαν ἀλλήλοις.

records.literal_gloss: If indeed therefore Demetrius and the with him craftsmen have against anyone a matter, courts are held and proconsuls there are; let them bring charges against one another.

en.L: So if Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a matter against anyone, court days are held and there are proconsuls; let them bring charges against one another.
en.B: So if Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a case against anyone, there are court days and there are proconsuls; let the parties bring their charges against each other there.
en.R: Demetrius and the men who work with him may have a complaint against someone. If so, they should take it to the courts. The courts meet on certain days, and there are proconsuls, the Roman governors, to judge. There they can accuse each other.

fr.L: Si donc Démétrius et les artisans qui sont avec lui ont une affaire contre quelqu’un, des audiences se tiennent et il y a des proconsuls ; qu’ils portent plainte les uns contre les autres.
fr.B: Si donc Démétrius et les artisans qui sont avec lui ont un grief contre quelqu’un, il y a des jours d’audience et il y a des proconsuls : que les parties y portent plainte l’une contre l’autre.
fr.R: Démétrius et les hommes qui travaillent avec lui ont peut-être une plainte contre quelqu’un. Si c’est le cas, ils doivent aller devant les tribunaux. Les tribunaux se réunissent certains jours, et il y a des proconsuls, les gouverneurs romains, pour juger. Là, ils pourront s’accuser les uns les autres.

es.L: Así que, si Demetrio y los artesanos que están con él tienen algún asunto contra alguien, hay días de audiencia y hay procónsules; que se acusen unos a otros.
es.B: Por tanto, si Demetrio y los artesanos que lo acompañan tienen alguna queja contra alguien, para eso hay días de audiencia y hay procónsules; que las partes presenten allí sus acusaciones unas contra otras.
es.R: Puede ser que Demetrio y los hombres que trabajan con él tengan una queja contra alguien. Si es así, deben llevarla a los tribunales. Los tribunales se reúnen ciertos días, y hay procónsules, los gobernadores romanos, para juzgar. Allí pueden acusarse unos a otros.

sw.L: Basi ikiwa Demetrio na mafundi walio pamoja naye wana shauri juu ya mtu yeyote, siku za mahakama zipo na wakuu wa majimbo wapo; na washtakiane.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, ikiwa Demetrio na mafundi walio pamoja naye wana shauri dhidi ya mtu yeyote, kuna siku za mahakama na kuna wakuu wa majimbo; pande hizo mbili na zishtakiane huko.
sw.R: Huenda Demetrio na watu wanaofanya kazi pamoja naye wana malalamiko dhidi ya mtu fulani. Ikiwa ndivyo, wanapaswa kuyapeleka mahakamani. Mahakama hukutana siku fulani, na kuna wakuu wa majimbo, yaani watawala wa Kirumi, wa kuhukumu. Huko wanaweza kushtakiana.

decisions.choice: court days are held: the courts sit on set days
decisions.reason: The word describes days when the courts met, often in the marketplace.

decisions.choice: proconsuls: the Roman governors of the province
decisions.reason: Asia was governed by one proconsul at a time. The plural speaks of the office in general: there are such officials to hear cases.

decisions.choice: bring charges against one another: let the two sides go to law
alternatives: accuse each other of the riot
decisions.reason: The verb means to accuse in court. The clerk sends the dispute to the courts.

decisions.choice: the Roman governors, to judge
decisions.reason: Readable says who the proconsuls were, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: εἰ δέ τι περαιτέρω ἐπιζητεῖτε, ἐν τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐπιλυθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: If however anything beyond this you seek, in the lawful assembly it will be settled.

en.L: But if you seek anything further, it will be settled in the lawful assembly.
en.B: Any further matter you raise will be dealt with in the lawful assembly.
en.R: If you want to deal with any other matter, it must be decided at a lawful meeting of the city assembly.

fr.L: Mais si vous cherchez quelque chose au-delà, cela sera réglé dans l’assemblée légale.
fr.B: Toute autre question que vous voudriez soulever sera réglée dans l’assemblée légale.
fr.R: Si vous voulez traiter une autre affaire, il faudra la décider lors d’une réunion légale de l’assemblée de la ville.

es.L: Y si {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} algo más, se resolverá en la asamblea legal.
es.B: Cualquier otro asunto que {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} plantear se resolverá en la asamblea legal.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} tratar algún otro asunto, tendrá que decidirse en una reunión legal de la asamblea de la ciudad.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa mnatafuta jambo lolote zaidi, litamalizwa katika mkutano halali.
sw.B: Jambo lingine lolote mtakalolileta litashughulikiwa katika mkutano halali.
sw.R: Ikiwa mnataka kushughulikia jambo lingine lolote, ni lazima liamuliwe katika mkutano halali wa wananchi wa mji.

decisions.choice: the lawful assembly: the regular assembly of citizens, called according to law
decisions.reason: The clerk sets the lawful assembly beside the confused gathering in the theater (19:32). Public matters belonged to the citizens' assembly when it met in proper order.

decisions.choice: anything further: matters beyond a charge against a person
alternatives: any more charges against these men
decisions.reason: Charges against persons go to the courts (19:38); public questions go to the assembly.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ κινδυνεύομεν ἐγκαλεῖσθαι στάσεως περὶ τῆς σήμερον μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος περὶ οὗ οὐ δυνησόμεθα ἀποδοῦναι λόγον περὶ τῆς συστροφῆς ταύτης.

records.literal_gloss: And for we are in danger of being accused of insurrection concerning the today, not one cause existing, concerning which not we will be able to give an account concerning the commotion this.

en.L: For indeed we are in danger of being accused of rioting over today's [events], there being no cause about which we will be able to give an account of this commotion."
en.B: Indeed, today's events put us in danger of being accused of rebellion. There is no cause we could point to, nothing we could say to explain this disorderly gathering."
en.R: We are in danger, because the Roman rulers could say that we started a riot today. There is no good reason for this crowd to be here. If they ask us about it, we will have nothing to say."

fr.L: Car nous risquons en effet d’être accusés d’émeute pour [les événements d’]aujourd’hui, puisqu’il n’existe aucun motif que nous pourrons invoquer pour rendre compte de cet attroupement. »
fr.B: En effet, les événements d’aujourd’hui nous exposent à être accusés de révolte. Il n’y a aucun motif que nous puissions avancer, rien que nous puissions dire pour expliquer ce rassemblement désordonné. »
fr.R: Nous sommes en danger, car les dirigeants romains pourraient dire que nous avons provoqué une émeute aujourd’hui. Il n’y a aucune bonne raison pour que cette foule soit ici. Si on nous pose des questions, nous n’aurons rien à répondre. »

es.L: Porque en verdad corremos peligro de ser acusados de sedición por lo de hoy, no habiendo ninguna causa por la cual podamos dar razón de este tumulto».
es.B: De hecho, por lo ocurrido hoy corremos el peligro de ser acusados de rebelión. No hay ninguna causa que podamos alegar, nada que podamos decir para explicar este tumulto».
es.R: Estamos en peligro, porque las autoridades romanas podrían decir que hoy comenzamos un motín. No hay ninguna buena razón para que esta multitud esté aquí. Si nos preguntan sobre esto, no tendremos nada que decir».

sw.L: Kwa maana kweli tuko hatarini kushtakiwa kwa uasi kwa sababu ya [mambo ya] leo, kwa kuwa hakuna sababu yoyote ambayo kwayo tutaweza kutoa maelezo juu ya ghasia hii."
sw.B: Kwa kweli matukio ya leo yanatuweka hatarini kushtakiwa kwa uasi. Hakuna sababu tunayoweza kuitaja, wala hakuna tunachoweza kusema kueleza mkusanyiko huu wa fujo."
sw.R: Tuko hatarini, kwa sababu watawala wa Kirumi wanaweza kusema kwamba tumeanzisha fujo leo. Hakuna sababu nzuri ya umati huu kuwa hapa. Wakituuliza habari zake, hatutakuwa na la kusema."

decisions.choice: insurrection: rioting, civil disorder
decisions.reason: The word means a rising or riot. Roman governors dealt harshly with cities that let crowds run riot, and a city could lose its privileges.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "about which we will not be able to give an account"
decisions.reason: With "not" the Greek has a double negative after "no cause", hard to put into words; without it the sentence reads more smoothly. Either way the sense is that they can give no reason for the gathering. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: commotion: a disorderly gathering, a mob
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd that has gathered together, here without lawful cause, set beside the lawful assembly (19:39).

decisions.choice: the Roman rulers could say
alternatives: we are in danger of being accused
decisions.reason: Readable names the likely accusers, whom the Greek leaves unnamed; the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: we will be able
decisions.reason: Literal leaves out the second negative of the Greek, which would reverse the sense in English; the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And these things having said he dismissed the assembly.

en.L: And having said these things, he dismissed the assembly.
en.B: With these words he sent the assembly away.
en.R: After he said this, he told the assembly to go home.

fr.L: Et ayant dit ces choses, il congédia l’assemblée.
fr.B: Sur ces mots, il renvoya l’assemblée.
fr.R: Après ces paroles, il a dit aux gens de l’assemblée de rentrer chez eux.

es.L: Y habiendo dicho estas cosas, disolvió la asamblea.
es.B: Dicho esto, despidió a la asamblea.
es.R: Después de decir esto, mandó a la gente de la asamblea a sus casas.

sw.L: Na akiisha kusema hayo, aliuvunja mkutano.
sw.B: Kwa maneno hayo aliuvunja mkutano.
sw.R: Baada ya kusema hayo, aliwaambia watu wa mkutano warudi nyumbani.

decisions.choice: the assembly: the gathering in the theater
decisions.reason: The same word as in 19:32 and 19:39. The clerk treats the crowd as an assembly and closes it.

decisions.choice: told the assembly to go home
decisions.reason: Readable says what dismissing meant.
